cards.text: We're back in Psalm 119, friend. The psalmist is still talking straight to the LORD, and he opens with this: "Oh, how I love Your law!" No warm-up, no small talk, just LOVE.

cards.question: The psalmist loves God's law. How much of his day does he spend meditating on it?

cards.text: Then he says God's commandments make him wiser than his enemies. Wiser than his enemies! Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer losing arguments to a twist tie.

cards.question: God's commandments make the psalmist wiser than his enemies. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The commandments are always with him
He is older than his enemies

cards.text: And he keeps going. He says he has more insight than ALL his teachers, and can you imagine saying that at work? To the people who TRAINED you?

cards.question: True or false: The psalmist says he has more insight than his teachers because he has traveled farther than they have.
The psalmist says he discerns more than the elders, because he ___ God's precepts.

cards.text: He says he's kept his feet from every evil path, so he can keep God's word. Me, I hop everywhere on this gold base and STILL end up face-first in the chocolate chips.

cards.question: True or false: The psalmist says he hasn't departed from God's ordinances because God Himself has taught him.

cards.text: Then he talks about how God's words taste. Yes, TASTE. I've been waiting this whole psalm for somebody to bring up flavor!

cards.question: How does the psalmist say God's words taste in his mouth?

cards.text: He says he gains understanding from God's precepts. And understanding does something to a man.

cards.question: Because he gains understanding from God's precepts, the psalmist hates every ___ way.

cards.text: And now the big one: "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path." Friend, I'd stamp that on every cookie in this bakery if I could fit the letters.

cards.question: The psalmist calls God's word a lamp to his feet and a light to his path. What's the picture?

answers.text: It shows him where to step
It keeps him warm through the night
It helps others find his house

cards.text: Then he says he has sworn and confirmed that he'll keep God's righteous judgments. That's not a "maybe, let me check my calendar." That's SWORN AND CONFIRMED.

cards.question: The psalmist says he is severely afflicted. He asks the LORD to revive him through His ___.

cards.text: Then he asks the LORD to accept the freewill offerings of his mouth. Offerings of his mouth! Mine mostly offers crumbs to the floor.

cards.question: Along with accepting his offerings, what does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Bring him back to the temple

cards.text: He says he constantly takes his life in his hands. Friend, I took my life in my hands every time somebody dug through that drawer looking for the scissors.

cards.question: Even with his life in his hands, the psalmist does not forget God's ___.

cards.text: Then he says the wicked have set a snare for him. Somebody out there is working OVERTIME to ruin this man's day.

cards.question: True or false: With a snare set for him, the psalmist says he has not strayed from God's precepts.
The psalmist calls God's testimonies his heritage forever. Why?

answers.text: They are the joy of his heart
The priests gave them to him

cards.question: True or false: The psalmist says he'll keep God's statutes only until his troubles are over.

cards.text: Then he says, "The double-minded I despise, but Your law I love." Double-minded. You know, the coworker who replies "I'm in" and "I'm out" in the SAME group chat.
Then he tells the LORD that He is his hiding place and his shield. A hiding place! Friend, I was a WORLD CHAMPION at hiding. Years in the back of a drawer, and nobody found me once.

cards.question: The psalmist calls the LORD his hiding place and his shield. What do both pictures say about God?
True or false: The psalmist says he puts his hope in his own strength.

cards.text: Then he turns and talks straight to the evildoers, and tells them to depart from him. Polite? No. Clear? VERY.

cards.question: Why does the psalmist tell the evildoers to depart from him?

answers.text: So he can obey God's commandments
So he can sleep in peace
So he can take back his land

cards.text: Then he asks the LORD to sustain him as He promised, so he may live. Not "if You have a minute." AS. YOU. PROMISED.

cards.question: As he asks the LORD to sustain him, the psalmist asks not to be ashamed of his ___.
The psalmist asks the LORD to uphold him. What does he say will happen then?

cards.text: Now he looks at everyone who strays from God's statutes, and he says the LORD rejects them ALL. Not most of them, not just the worst ones, ALL.

cards.question: True or false: The psalmist says the deceitfulness of those who stray from God's statutes is in vain.

cards.text: Then he says the LORD discards all the wicked on earth like dross. Strong words. Now watch what the psalmist does with them.

cards.question: The LORD discards the wicked like dross. What does the psalmist say he does because of that?

cards.text: He ends this part honest: his flesh trembles, and he stands in fear of the LORD's judgments. No big finish, friend, just a man shaking in his sandals.

cards.question: The psalmist says his flesh trembles in ___ of the LORD.

cards.text: Keep the oven warm on this one, friend. Psalm 119 still has plenty more to say.

The baker leaves without the actual reason, even though the reasons in 98 to 100 drive this part of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke's action does not match the verse. In 119:114, a hiding place is a refuge where you are kept safe. Papa Dorin's 'hiding' in the drawer was being forgotten and left in the dark. Those are two different actions, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Nobody found me once' adds something new to the backstory and goes against it. In the backstory, the angel opens the drawer and calls him out, and the backstory says he 'knows what it's like to be found.'

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The final 'story isn't over' card tells no verse, but it cites Psalm 119:120. That verse was already told on card 14. The rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, no wider and no narrower. This card tells none.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it carries only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse: the passage's last verse, the whole passage range, or something else?
